title: aiPHeed window study v3: approved period 2021-2026, corrected data, pre-registered
status_at_writing: No model has been run on the 2021+ frame. Only the label median (14.345) and the feasibility numbers below were computed.
scope_note: Researcher instruction 2026-10-09: approved study period is 2021-2026. The extracted Chapter III text (THESIS 2 (9).pdf) states 2020-Q1..2025-Q4; this discrepancy is flagged for the adviser, and the researcher's instruction is followed.

window_rule_W.labels: target quarters >= 2021-Q1 only (16 labelled quarters, 80 rows; 2026 has no released SWS round, so no 2026 labels)
window_rule_W.features: every value whose reference period is before 2021-Q1 is excluded (missing): 2020 government observations (including the t-1 values that strict timing would take from 2020-Q4), 2020 news, 2020 SWS rounds, the 2018 poverty survey (used through 2022-Q3), and any lag/accel/rolling statistic that would reach into 2020
window_rule_W.allowed_reference_bases: published statistics for 2021+ reference periods are kept even when defined relative to a base: CPI 2018=100 index and its published YoY rates, rainfall anomalies against the WMO 1991-2020 normal (flagged for adviser)
window_rule_W.release_dates: strict Rule 3 timing unchanged: government series of t-1, news of t, SWS latest round released before t+1, poverty as released

new_features_pre_declared.sws_change: latest released SWS round minus the previous released round (both >= 2021-Q1, both released before t+1)
new_features_pre_declared.sws_age: quarters between the latest released SWS round and the target quarter
new_features_pre_declared.rice_retail_regular, rice_retail_well: PSA OpenStat provincial retail RMR and WMR (psa_indicators; previously unused), t-1
new_features_pre_declared.news_ph_fssi, news_ph_count: mean Algorithm-1 score and count of ALL retained (>= 0.30) articles in quarter t regardless of province (national/regional news pool; same scoring, no new model)

target.primary: Eq. 3 definition applied to the approved period: HIGH if stress > global median of the 80 labelled 2021-2025 rows = 14.345 (differs from 14.6 on 1 row)
target.disclosure: the global median uses all labelled rows including the test quarters, as Eq. 3 specifies

outer_protocol: expanding window, minimum 8 labelled target quarters -> 8 outer test quarters 2023-Q3..2025-Q4 (40 rows), seed 42, cut-off 0.50; these 40 rows are a subset of rows used in earlier studies (disclosed)
primary_estimand: Outer mean quarter accuracy of nested procedure P4 (pool below; inner walk-forward, minimum 5 inner quarters, training rows only; exact ties -> earliest in pool order)
pool_P4_order: struct_rule: HIGH if sws_hunger + 2*cpi_rel > label threshold (no fitting)

feature sets in order: struct2 [sws_hunger, cpi_rel]; struct5 [sws_hunger, sws_change, sws_age, cpi_rel, cpi_rel_lag1]; eq5_struct; gov_c; gov_c_plus (gov_c + rice_retail_regular, rice_retail_well, news_ph_fssi, news_ph_count)
families per set: logistic L2 C {0.01,0.1,1,10} x {none,balanced}; tree depth {1,2,3} leaf 5 x {none,balanced}; LightGBM {small,default} x {none, scale_pos_weight}
descriptive_only: MODEL-B2 config (gov_c, spw) and MODEL-A config (eq5) on the 2021+ frame
timing-valid persistence (recomputed with 2021+ labels and the primary threshold)

acceptance_rule.C2: one-sided 95% lower bounds >= 0.75 (quarter bootstrap AND Clopper-Pearson)
acceptance_rule.C3: beats timing-valid persistence AND clock-only (bootstrap p5 > 0)
acceptance_rule.C5: 2026 quarters scored when SWS releases them, using forecasts frozen in this study before any 2026 label is seen

prospective_2026: Train each frozen candidate on all labelled 2021-2025 rows and issue forecasts for every 2026 quarter whose origin data exist in the project (2026-Q1, 2026-Q2). Hash and store them now; score only after SWS publishes the rounds. Forecasts are issued late but label-blind; input vintages are current, not as-released.
commitment: P4's score is the reported primary result whatever it is; no pool or correction change after outer results are seen.
